coverage_of_risk.rationale: The app wrote zero tests, so none of its riskiest logic — data mapping, URL state parsing, sorting — is covered by anything it owns.

evidence: app/src — no test files exist anywhere under app/
behaviour_not_implementation.rationale: No tests at all, so nothing to assess; the pure helpers in api.ts/moves.ts are well-positioned for behaviour-level unit tests but were left untested.

evidence: app/src/lib/api.ts:96 — MAX_SPECIES_ID boundary and species fallback have no guard
app/src/pages/index.astro:27-29 — clamp/parseInt edge cases (page=0, page=999, NaN) have no guard

regression_power.rationale: With no app-owned tests, any refactor that breaks the behaviours above passes the app's own (empty) suite; only the external acceptance suite would catch a subset.

evidence: app/package.json:6-10 — no test runner, no devDependencies for testing
signal_to_noise.rationale: No tests means no noise, but also no signal; per the anchor this scores neutral.

findings.issue: No test infrastructure at all: no test script, no runner (Vitest), no test files, despite a data layer (api.ts, moves.ts) purpose-built as pure, easily testable helpers.
findings.suggestion: Add Vitest with unit tests for api.ts helpers and moves.ts table construction, plus a small Playwright config for the client-side scripts; wire into npm test in app/package.json.

findings.issue: pokemonRefsToSpecies — the id < 10000 alternate-form exclusion, dedup, and species-name fallback are unpinned; a refactor flipping the comparison or dropping the fallback would link deoxys-normal URLs from type/move/ability pages.
findings.suggestion: Unit tests against fixture refs: alternate form (id 10001), deoxys-normal (386), duplicate entries, and a ref whose species is absent from the species list.

findings.issue: URL state parsing is untested: page clamping (page=999 → last page, page=abc → 1), invalid type/generation silently ignored, and pageHref omitting defaults (page 1) — a refactor could break deep links or duplicate query params.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test the filter/clamp/href logic by extracting it from the frontmatter into lib and covering out-of-range, NaN, unknown-filter and default-omission cases.

findings.issue: Sort comparator's missing-values-last rule bypasses the direction sign by design; a cleanup that applies sign uniformly (or uses the raw dataset value) breaks descending sort for blank Power/Accuracy cells, and string/numeric mixing (data-value '10' vs '9') can regress silently.
findings.suggestion: Extract the comparator into a testable function and pin: missing last in both directions, numeric vs lexicographic, tie-break stability.

findings.issue: Client filter script (debounce, AbortController, DOMParser swap, popstate resync) is untested DOM logic; races between typing and select changes or a broken popstate sync would only surface as intermittent UI bugs.
findings.suggestion: A Playwright test driving search typing, filter changes, and back/forward navigation asserting both URL and rendered results.

findings.issue: No test pins error behaviour when the API errors (non-404): getJson throws and the whole page 500s; when the 60s cache holds a rejected-then-evicted promise a subsequent request refetches — unverified eviction path at api.ts:45.
findings.suggestion: Unit test getJson against 404 (→ null), 500 (→ throw), and cache eviction after failure using a stubbed fetch.

findings.issue: Unknown ?game=bogus silently falls back to the latest game instead of erroring; dedup key and version-group ordering by `order` are untested.
findings.suggestion: Unit test getMoveTables with a small pokemon fixture: method order (level-up, machine, egg, tutor, then others), level-up rows ordered by level then name, invalid game fallback.

findings.issue: Cache behaviour unpinned: expired entries are never pruned (unbounded Map growth), 404 nulls are cached for 60s, and concurrent identical requests share one promise — any of these could change in refactor with no signal.
findings.suggestion: Unit tests with fake timers covering TTL expiry, 404 caching, and single-flight behaviour.

summary: The app shipped with zero tests of its own despite having extracted its trickiest logic (species mapping, move-table construction, URL state, table sorting) into pure, highly testable modules — a missed opportunity, not a structural barrier. Once the acceptance suite stops being the only guard, refactors to these areas have no safety net and the most likely regressions are boundary bugs in the alternate-form filter, pagination clamps, and the missing-values sort rule. Add Vitest unit tests for lib/ and a handful of Playwright tests for the two client-side scripts.
